name: Alma vs SonderMind
title: Alma vs SonderMind: Provider Network Comparison for Therapists (2026)
description: Compare Alma and SonderMind provider platforms for insurance credentialing and billing. See differences in pricing, features, reimbursement rates, and platform fairness for mental health providers.

summary.bottom_line: Alma charges $95-125/month but includes AI notes, EHR, and weekly pay with potentially higher reimbursement rates. SonderMind is free to join but has concerning provider reviews (2.3/5 compensation rating on Glassdoor) and only one rate increase in 4.5 years. Both platforms retain your credentials if you leave. Consider the total value proposition: Alma costs more but offers more features; SonderMind is free but has rate stability concerns.

sections.heading: Alma vs SonderMind: Overview
sections.content: Alma and SonderMind are two of the largest provider networks helping therapists accept insurance. Alma charges a membership fee ($95-125/month) but bundles AI notes, EHR, scheduling, peer consultation, and claims to negotiate higher reimbursement rates. SonderMind is free to join but provides fewer tools-it's primarily credentialing and billing. Spring Health acquired Alma in January 2026. Both platforms work with major insurers (Aetna, Cigna, UnitedHealthcare, BCBS) but neither gives you portable credentials if you leave.

sections.heading: Pricing and Cost Analysis
sections.content: SonderMind is free, period. Alma costs $125/month or $95/month with annual billing. Is Alma worth the cost? Alma claims to negotiate $10-30 higher per-session rates than solo credentialing. At 20 sessions/week, even a $10 rate improvement generates $800/month in additional revenue-more than covering membership. However, one therapist reported Optum paid Alma $151 for a session they received $110.30 for (27% spread). Factor in both the membership fee and the fee spread when calculating true costs.

sections.heading: Feature Comparison
sections.content: Alma offers significantly more features: Note Assist (AI session notes), full EHR with assessments and treatment plans, peer consultation groups, access to clinical advisors (Esther Perel, Lori Gottlieb), and community events. SonderMind's feature set is leaner-primarily insurance credentialing, billing, provider directory, and continuing education. The $500 referral bonus (Alma) incentivizes network growth. SonderMind's VA partnership is notable if you want to serve veterans (100% covered).

sections.heading: Provider Fairness Concerns
sections.content: Both platforms have concerning fairness issues. SonderMind has a 2.3/5 Glassdoor compensation rating (very low), with reviews citing 'insulting' pay and only one rate increase in 4.5 years. SonderMind raised client out-of-pocket by $30/session in Arizona but gave providers $0 of that increase. Alma faced 2024 Optum rate cuts of up to 30% ($7-43/session reduction) and 2026 Aetna cuts affecting psychologists. Neither platform gives you portable credentials-if you leave, you lose panel access and must re-credential from scratch.

sections.heading: Payment and Reimbursement
sections.content: Alma pays weekly; SonderMind pays bi-weekly with a same-day option. Reported reimbursement rates vary: Alma therapists report $100-120/session after platform fees, while SonderMind therapists report $72-98/hour. Indeed data shows SonderMind therapists average $102,900/year (56% above national average), though wide variance exists ($24,000-$125,000 range). Alma's rate stability has been affected by payer cuts; SonderMind's rates have been largely frozen.

recommendations.when: You want AI session notes and full EHR included; you value peer consultation and community features; you can see 20+ sessions/week to justify the membership cost; or you prefer weekly payments over bi-weekly

You want zero upfront cost (free to join); you want to serve VA beneficiaries (100% covered); you accept Medicare/Medicare Advantage patients; or you have low session volume where Alma's membership doesn't pencil out
You want a free platform with potentially better provider satisfaction-consider comparing Headway to both before deciding
You want portable credentials that stay with you, not the platform-this requires more work but gives you ownership

faqs.q: Is Alma or SonderMind free for therapists?
faqs.a: SonderMind is free to join. Alma costs $125/month or $95/month with annual billing ($1,140/year). However, Alma claims to negotiate higher reimbursement rates that can offset the membership cost for providers with sufficient session volume.

faqs.q: Do I keep my credentials if I leave Alma or SonderMind?
faqs.a: No. With both platforms, credentials belong to the platform, not you. If you leave Alma or SonderMind, you lose panel access and must re-credential from scratch on your own. Consider dual-credentialing independently if building a long-term practice.

faqs.q: Which has better reimbursement rates: Alma or SonderMind?
faqs.a: Reported rates vary. Alma therapists report $100-120/session; SonderMind therapists report $72-98/hour. Alma claims $10-30 higher rates than solo credentialing, but their fee spread and membership cost reduce net income. SonderMind is free but has concerning rate stability (only 1 increase in 4.5 years).

faqs.q: Does Alma or SonderMind include AI notes?
faqs.a: Only Alma includes AI session notes (Note Assist) as part of the membership. SonderMind does not include AI documentation-you would need a separate AI scribe tool like Mentalyc or Upheal.

faqs.q: Can I see veterans through Alma or SonderMind?
faqs.a: SonderMind has a VA partnership where therapy is 100% covered for veterans with a valid VA referral, available in all 50 states. Alma does not have a comparable VA partnership.
